speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with agitation, yellowish skin and eyes, and abnormal lab results. To determine the cause of this jaundice, can you tell me how long you have noticed these symptoms and if you have experienced any abdominal pain or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis A (Hepatitis A virus infection)

The patient's young age, acute onset of jaundice over a week, agitation due to hepatic encephalopathy, and history of high-risk sexual behaviors strongly suggest a viral etiology. While substance use and alcohol are present, they are less likely to cause such rapid fulminant hepatitis in a previously healthy 20-year-old without a longer history of heavy drinking. I will request specific liver function tests and viral serology to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Test (AST, ALT, Bilirubin, Alkaline Phosphatase), Hepatitis_A_IgM, Hepatitis_B_Surface_Antigen, Hepatitis_C_Antibody.
